en.stem: For each branch, state its main subject of study: cytology, histology, genetics, ecology and pharmacology.
en.answer: Cytology: cells and their structures. Histology: tissues examined microscopically. Genetics: inheritance of characteristics. Ecology: relationships between organisms and their environment. Pharmacology: drugs and their effects on the body.

en.stem: Explain how biology connects with chemistry, physics, statistics, computing and economics. Give the corresponding biological field for each.
en.answer: Biochemistry studies chemical substances and reactions in living systems. Biophysics applies physical principles to biological processes. Biostatistics interprets biological data statistically. Computational biology uses models, algorithms and simulations. Bio-economics examines the cost and profit of biological projects.

en.stem: Explain interdisciplinary collaboration using the Human Genome Project as an example. State the project aim and the contributions of genetics, molecular biology and computing.
en.answer: Interdisciplinary collaboration combines expertise from different fields. The Human Genome Project aimed to sequence and map the human genome. en.stem: Describe five steps following recognition of a scientific problem: observation, hypothesis, deduction, experiment and reporting results.
en.answer: Observation gathers relevant information. A hypothesis proposes a testable explanation. A deduction predicts an outcome if that explanation is correct. An experiment tests the prediction. Results are analysed, summarised and shared so others can examine the findings.

en.stem: Outline the textbook investigation of the cause of malaria using five headings: observation, hypothesis, deduction, comparison and conclusion.
en.answer: Observation: Plasmodium was seen in patient blood. Hypothesis: this parasite causes malaria. Deduction: the parasite should occur in malaria-patient blood. Comparison: patient and healthy-person blood samples were examined microscopically. Conclusion: the reported findings supported the proposed association between Plasmodium and malaria.
